flags.why: This jar name is used mainly in Southern Vietnamese ([regional vocabulary discussion](https://nguvan.hnue.edu.vn/Nghi%C3%AAn-c%E1%BB%A9u/Ng%C3%B4n-ng%E1%BB%AF/p/1813)).
The example explains what surfing is instead of showing someone using the word in context.
flags.fix: Cuối tuần, tôi thường đi lướt sóng. = I often go surfing at weekends.

flags.why: Cả người means the whole body here, not all of us.
flags.fix: On the high hill, the strong wind cooled my whole body.

flags.why: In this drainage context, cầu refers to toilets, so the gloss incorrectly presents both components as drainage pipes ([usage example](https://thongcaucongdanang.vn/dung-cu-thong-tac-cau-cong/)).

Cầu cống does not mean the plumbing trade; its established occupational use concerns bridges and culverts ([dictionary entry](https://vtudien.com/viet-viet/dictionary/nghia-cua-tu-c%E1%BA%A7u%20c%E1%BB%91ng)).
This expression is mainly Southern Vietnamese ([Southern vocabulary list](https://conganhuynh.com/TuNguMienNam.htm)).
